title.zh: 卷380 列傳一百六十七 陈若霖 戴三锡 孙尔准 程祖洛 马济胜 裕泰 贺长龄
title.en: Volume 380 Biographies 167: Chen Ruolin, Dai Sanxi, Sun Erzhun, Cheng Zuluo, Ma Jisheng, Yu Tai, He Zhangling
title.raw: 卷380 列傳一百六十七 陈若霖 戴三锡 孙尔准 程祖洛 马济胜 裕泰 贺长龄

sentences.zh: 列傳一百六十七

translations.literal: Biographies 167
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 167

sentences.zh: 陳若霖戴三錫孫爾準程祖洛馬濟勝裕泰賀長齡

translations.literal: Chen Ruolin, Dai Sanxi, Sun Erzhun, Cheng Zuluo, Ma Jisheng, Yu Tai, He Zhangling
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruolin, Dai Sanxi, Sun Erzhun, Cheng Zuluo, Ma Jisheng, Yu Tai, and He Zhangling

sentences.zh: 陳若霖，字宗覲，福建閩縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Ruolin, style name Zongqin, was a native of Min County, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruolin, whose style name was Zongqin, came from Min County in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授刑部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of the Qianlong reign he became a metropolitan graduate, was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, and upon completing his probation was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice; he was promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1787, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after completing his probation was posted as a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, rising eventually to director.

sentences.zh: 束鹿縣民王洪中為人聚毆，訟不得直，自經死。

translations.literal: Wang Hongzhong, a commoner of Shulu County, was beaten in a mob attack; his lawsuit failed to obtain justice, and he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hongzhong, a man of Shulu County, was set upon and beaten by a crowd, he could obtain no redress in court and hanged himself in despair.

sentences.zh: 若霖鞫得其實，被議敘。

translations.literal: Ruolin tried the case and established the facts; he was subject to a merit review.
translations.idiomatic: Ruolin investigated the case, established what had happened, and was commended in the official merit review.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當外用，仍留部。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he should have been sent to serve outside the capital, but he remained in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Although his term entitled him to an outside appointment, he was kept on at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 數從大臣赴各省讞獄，以寬恕稱。

translations.literal: He repeatedly accompanied senior officials to review criminal cases in the provinces and was known for leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He often accompanied senior ministers on provincial criminal reviews and earned a reputation for clemency.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年，出為四川鹽茶道，擢山東按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Jiaqing reign he went out as Sichuan Salt and Tea Circuit intendant and was promoted to Shandong surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 he left the capital as intendant of the Sichuan Salt and Tea Circuit and was soon promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 調廣東，署布政使，以佐總督百齡平海盜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong as acting administration commissioner; for assisting Governor-General Bai Ling in suppressing pirates he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangdong as acting administration commissioner, he aided Governor-General Bai Ling in suppressing piracy and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 調湖北，復調四川，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hubei, then back to Sichuan, and was promoted in place to administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After postings in Hubei and then Sichuan again, he was promoted on the spot to administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815 he was appointed governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 水尾土州目黃金珠結內地奸民，殺副州目李文政，掠其家，鞫實，置於法。

translations.literal: Huang Jinzhu, native chieftain of Shuiwei Tuzhou, joined with inland ruffians, killed Vice-Chieftain Li Wenzheng, and plundered his household; the facts were established at trial and he was punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jinzhu, the native chieftain of Shuiwei, colluded with mainland criminals to murder Vice-Chieftain Li Wenzheng and loot his family; once the case was proved, Huang was executed according to law.

sentences.zh: 歷廣東、河南、浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: He served successively as governor of Guangdong, Henan, and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to govern Guangdong, Henan, and Zhejiang in turn.

sentences.zh: 浙省南北新關科罰無度，限以半正額為止，卹商而課裕。

translations.literal: At the northern and southern new customs posts of Zhejiang, fines were levied without limit; he capped them at half the regular quota, relieving merchants while keeping revenue sound.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhejiang's northern and southern new customs houses, penalties had been exacted without restraint; he capped them at half the statutory rate, easing the burden on merchants while keeping revenue healthy.

sentences.zh: 修蕭山新廟堤，建盤頭以御潮。

translations.literal: He repaired the Xinmiao embankment at Xiaoshan and built a spur dike to resist the tide.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Xinmiao dike at Xiaoshan and built a headwork to break the tidal surge.

sentences.zh: 次年，新林塘圮，親往勘，疏言：「新林塘舊為險工，今距海日遠，塘以外為灶地，外復為牧地，中有馬塘，足為新林屏蔽，宜補築以遏潮汐。

translations.literal: The next year the Xinlin embankment collapsed; he went in person to inspect it and memorialized: "The Xinlin embankment was formerly a critical work; now the sea is daily farther off. Beyond the embankment are salt-pan lands, and beyond those pasture lands; between them is Matang, which can serve as a screen for Xinlin. It should be repaired to check the tide."
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Xinlin seawall failed; he inspected the site himself and reported: "Xinlin was once a critical floodwork, but the shoreline has receded. Beyond the wall lie salt flats, then pasture, with Matang in between—enough to shield Xinlin. The wall should be rebuilt to hold back the tide."

sentences.zh: 疏通灶地各溝洫，引入牧地之莫家等灣以排泄之，即以灶地之土培護新林堤基。

translations.literal: The ditches of the salt-pan lands should be cleared and led into bays such as Mojia in the pasture lands for drainage, and the soil of the salt-pan lands should be used to strengthen the Xinlin dike foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed clearing the salt-flat ditches and channeling runoff into bays such as Mojia on the pasture side, then using the excavated soil to buttress the Xinlin dike.

sentences.zh: 西築橫塘以御江水。

translations.literal: To the west, build a transverse embankment to resist the river water.
translations.idiomatic: On the west, a cross-dike should be built to hold back the river.

sentences.zh: 責令灶牧各戶及蕭山、山陰、會稽三縣，分別修築。

translations.literal: The salt-pan and pasture households and the three counties of Xiaoshan, Shanyin, and Kuaiji should be ordered to carry out the repairs respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Salt producers, herders, and the counties of Xiaoshan, Shanyin, and Kuaiji should each be assigned their share of the work.

sentences.zh: 」又奏修會稽、上虞等縣塘堤，並如議行。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized on repairing the seawalls and dikes of Kuaiji, Shangyu, and other counties, and all was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " He also petitioned to repair the seawalls of Kuaiji, Shangyu, and neighboring counties; the plan was approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1819 he was appointed governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 湖南鳳凰等廳屯丁額多為官佔，失業者眾，悉清釐發還徵租。

translations.literal: In Hunan, at Fenghuang and other garrisons, many military colonist quotas had been seized by officials, leaving many without livelihood; he cleared the accounts entirely, restored the quotas, and collected rent.
translations.idiomatic: At Fenghuang and other Hunan garrisons, official encroachment had stripped many military colonists of their allotments; he investigated thoroughly, restored the quotas, and resumed rent collection.

sentences.zh: 官入苗寨多婪索，或冒名詐財，嚴禁之。

translations.literal: When officials entered Miao stockades they often extorted greedily or used false names to defraud for money; he strictly forbade this.
translations.idiomatic: Officials entering Miao villages had grown notorious for extortion and impersonation scams; he banned such abuses outright.

sentences.zh: 又以屯地磽瘠租額重，為奏減苗租二萬餘石，免逋賦七萬餘石，苗民感之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the garrison lands were poor and barren yet the rent quotas were heavy, he memorialized to reduce Miao rent by more than twenty thousand piculs and remit more than seventy thousand piculs of arrears; the Miao people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Finding garrison lands barren yet heavily taxed, he secured reductions of more than twenty thousand piculs in Miao rent and remission of over seventy thousand piculs in arrears, winning deep gratitude among the Miao.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，調四川。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Daoguang reign he was transferred to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was transferred to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 中江覃萬典、犍為道士蕭來修等假神惑眾，捕誅首犯，不坐株連。

translations.literal: Tan Wandian of Zhongjiang, the Daoist Xiao Laixiu of Qianwei, and others feigned divine powers to delude the masses; the ringleaders were arrested and executed without extending guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Wandian of Zhongjiang, the Qianwei Daoist Xiao Laixiu, and others had posed as divinities to mislead crowds; Ruolin seized and executed the leaders without punishing their followers by association.

sentences.zh: 九姓長官司不諳吏治，奏請考試，獄訟別由瀘州及州判兼理。

translations.literal: The Nine-Surname Native Officialdom was unversed in civil administration; he memorialized requesting examinations, with lawsuits to be handled separately by Luzhou and the subprefectural judge.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine-Surname chieftains were ill-equipped for civil governance; he petitioned for qualifying examinations and for Luzhou and its subprefectural judge to handle their legal cases.

sentences.zh: 四年，召授工部尚書，調刑部，兼管順天府尹事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned and appointed minister of works, transferred to the Ministry of Justice, and concurrently managed the affairs of the Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was recalled to the capital as minister of works, moved to the Ministry of Justice, and given concurrent charge of the Shuntian metropolitan magistracy.

sentences.zh: 文安縣地形如釜底，自道光初堤防衝決，積水不能耕種，議請急行修築。

translations.literal: Wen'an County's terrain is like the bottom of a cauldron; since the beginning of the Daoguang reign the dikes have burst, water has accumulated, and fields cannot be cultivated; he proposed urgent repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an lies in a natural basin; since the Daoguang reign began, breached dikes had left fields waterlogged and untilled, and he urged immediate reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 七年，命勘湖北京山黃家陵堤工，疏言：「下游災民籥請修治潰堤，上游居民謂口門下游乃襄河故道，復請廢之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to inspect the Huangjialing dike works at Jingshan in northern Huguang and memorialized: "Downstream disaster victims urgently petition to repair the breached dike, while upstream residents say the area below the breach mouth is the old course of the Xiang River and again petition to abandon it."
translations.idiomatic: In 1827 he was sent to survey the Huangjialing dike at Jingshan in northern Huguang and reported: "Downstream flood victims pleaded to repair the breach, while upstream residents insisted the channel below the gap was the old Xiang River bed and demanded it be left open."

sentences.zh: 河流經行二百餘年，捨此不由，而別尋二百年以前故道，其說殊謬。

translations.literal: The river has followed this course for more than two hundred years; to abandon it and seek instead a channel from two hundred years ago is utterly mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The river has run this way for over two centuries; to abandon the present channel and reopen a two-hundred-year-old bed is absurd.

sentences.zh: 潛江、天門、漢川俱屬下游，而天門、漢川尤當衝要，何忍委之巨浸？

translations.literal: Qianjiang, Tianmen, and Hanchuan all lie downstream, and Tianmen and Hanchuan especially stand at critical points—how can we bear to abandon them to vast inundation?
translations.idiomatic: Qianjiang, Tianmen, and Hanchuan all lie downstream, with Tianmen and Hanchuan at the most vulnerable points—how could we condemn them to wholesale flooding?

sentences.zh: 惟有開通江流，堵合口門，因勢利導。

translations.literal: The only course is to open the river flow, close the breach mouth, and guide the water according to its natural tendency.
translations.idiomatic: The answer is to clear the main channel, seal the breach, and guide the current along its natural course.

sentences.zh: 胡家灣沙洲當下游之衝，以四十餘丈之地束全江之水，下壅上潰，理有必然。

translations.literal: The sandbar at Hujiawan lies in the path of the downstream current; to confine the entire river within some forty-plus zhang of space causes blockage below and breach above—as a matter of course.
translations.idiomatic: The Hujiawan sandbar blocks the lower reach; squeezing the full river through barely forty zhang inevitably dams the flow below and forces breaches upstream.

sentences.zh: 今洲已衝潰，乘勢挑濬新灘，展寬水道，使江流無衝突之患，然後增築京山、鍾祥口門堤壩，再於潰口築石壩二，以護堤攻沙，庶可經久。

translations.literal: Now the bar has been washed away; taking advantage of this, dredge the new shoal, widen the channel, and remove the river's conflicting hazards; then heighten the dike dams at the breach mouths of Jingshan and Zhongxiang, and further build two stone dams at the breach to protect the dikes and attack the silt—only then can the works endure.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the bar has washed away, he urged dredging the new shoal and widening the channel to end the choke point, then raising the Jingshan and Zhongxiang breach dikes and building two stone dams at the gap to shield the embankments and scour away silt—a durable fix.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，乞休歸，卒於途，賜卹。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he requested retirement and return home; he died on the road and was granted funeral compensation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he asked to retire and died on the journey home; the court granted funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 戴三錫，順天大興人，原籍江蘇丹徒。

translations.literal: Dai Sanxi was a native of Daxing, Shuntian, with original domicile in Dantu, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sanxi was registered in Daxing, Shuntian, though his family hailed from Dantu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，授山西臨縣知縣。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the fifty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign, he was appointed magistrate of Lin County, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the metropolitan examination in 1793, he was appointed magistrate of Lin County in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 連丁父母憂，嘉慶六年，服闋，發四川，補南充。

translations.literal: He observed mourning in succession for both parents; in the sixth year of Jiaqing, when mourning ended, he was dispatched to Sichuan and appointed to Nanchong.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned both parents in turn; when his mourning ended in 1801 he was sent to Sichuan and posted to Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 歷馬邊、瓘邊兩廳通判，署資州、眉州、卭州，並有政聲。

translations.literal: He served as subprefect of Mabian and Fanbian departments, and acted as prefect of Zizhou, Meizhou, and Qiongzhou, winning a reputation for good governance in each post.
translations.idiomatic: He served as subprefect on the Mabian and Fanbian frontier circuits and as acting prefect of Zizhou, Meizhou, and Qiongzhou, earning praise for sound administration wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 卭州民黃子賢以治病為名，倡立鴻鈞教，捕治之。

translations.literal: Huang Zixian, a commoner of Qiongzhou, under the pretext of healing founded the Hongjun sect; Sanxi arrested and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Zixian of Qiongzhou used medical practice as a cover to found the Hongjun sect, Sanxi seized and punished him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，仁宗命送部引見，擢茂州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Jiaqing Emperor ordered him sent to the ministry for imperial audience and promoted him to magistrate of Maozhou Direct Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor, hearing of the case, ordered Sanxi to the capital for an audience and promoted him to magistrate of Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 歷寧遠知府、建昌道、四川按察使。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Ningyuan, Jianchang circuit intendant, and Sichuan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Ningyuan prefect, Jianchang circuit intendant, and Sichuan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，遷江寧布政使，迴避本籍，仍調四川。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was moved to Jiangning administration commissioner; to avoid his native place he was transferred back to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was named Jiangning administration commissioner, but to avoid serving in his home province was sent back to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，署總督，五年，實授，兼署成都將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he acted as governor-general; in the fifth year he received the substantive appointment and concurrently acted as Chengdu regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he served as acting governor-general; in 1825 he received the full appointment and also acted as regional commander at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 三錫自牧令洊陟封疆，二十餘年，未離蜀地。

translations.literal: Sanxi rose from magistrate and prefect step by step to frontier governor; for more than twenty years he never left Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Sanxi had climbed from county magistrate to frontier governor over more than twenty years without ever leaving Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 盡心民事，興復通省書院，增設義學三千餘所。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to the people's affairs, restored the provincial academy, and added more than three thousand charity schools.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into civil administration, restored the provincial academy, and founded more than three thousand charity schools across the province.

sentences.zh: 四川舊有義田，積儲備賑，穀多則變價添置良田。

translations.literal: Sichuan had long had charity fields whose accumulated stores were kept for relief; when grain was abundant it was sold and the proceeds used to buy more fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's charity estates had long stockpiled grain for famine relief, selling surplus grain to buy more fertile land when stores grew large.

sentences.zh: 三錫以歲久將膏腴多成官產，留穀太多，又虞霉變虧挪，差定三千至萬石為額。

translations.literal: Sanxi held that over the years fertile land had largely become official property, too much grain was retained, and there was fear of mold, spoilage, and embezzlement; he fixed a quota of three thousand to ten thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Sanxi found that over time the best charity lands had been absorbed as official property, stores had grown excessive, and grain risked spoilage and theft; he capped reserves at three thousand to ten thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 溢額者出糶，價存司庫，以備兇歲賑恤之用。

translations.literal: Surplus above the quota was sold off, the proceeds kept in the provincial treasury for use in famine years for relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: Any surplus was sold and the proceeds held in the provincial treasury for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 又以蜀地惟成都附近俱平疇沃野，餘多山谷磽瘠，遇水沖塞，膏腴轉為砂石，因地制宜，多設渠堰，以資捍衛宣洩。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Shu only the vicinity of Chengdu has level fields and rich soil; elsewhere there are mostly valleys and barren hills, and when water rushes and silts, fertile land turns to sand and stone; adapting to local conditions, he built many canals and weirs for defense and drainage.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Chengdu plain, Sichuan is mostly rugged and poor; flash floods could turn fertile soil to gravel, so he built canals and weirs suited to each locality for irrigation and flood control.

sentences.zh: 新都奸民楊守一倡立邪教，造妖書惑眾，擒誅之。

translations.literal: The ruffian Yang Shouyi of Xindu founded a heterodox sect and composed demon writings to delude the masses; he was seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xindu agitator Yang Shouyi founded a heterodox cult and circulated seditious tracts, Sanxi captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 越巂生番劫奪商旅，掠漢民婦女，捕駔黠者數十人置之法，救出被掠男婦，給貲安撫。

translations.literal: The raw tribes of Yuexi plundered merchants and travelers and seized Han women; he arrested several dozen of the craftiest ringleaders and punished them by law, rescued the abducted men and women, and gave funds to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuexi tribesmen had been robbing travelers and abducting Han women; he arrested dozens of the ringleaders, freed the captives, and compensated them for their losses.

sentences.zh: 屢被詔褒獎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly commended by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: The throne repeatedly commended him by edict.

sentences.zh: 九年，因年老召來京，署工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because of age he was summoned to the capital and appointed acting vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1829, on account of his age, he was recalled to the capital as acting vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕，未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he retired from office; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired from office and died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其「宣力有年，官聲素好」，贈尚書銜，依贈銜賜卹。

translations.literal: An edict praised him: "For years he has discharged his duties; his official reputation has always been good," and granted him the honorary rank of minister, with funeral compensation according to that rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his "years of devoted service and consistently fine reputation," posthumously granted him ministerial rank, and awarded funeral honors accordingly.

sentences.zh: 孫爾準，字平叔，江蘇金匱人，廣西巡撫永清子。

translations.literal: Sun Erzhun, style name Pingshu, was a native of Jingui, Jiangsu, and son of Yongqing, governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Erzhun, style name Pingshu, came from Jingui in Jiangsu and was the son of Yongqing, former governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the tenth year of Jiaqing, he was selected as Hanlin Bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in 1805, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出為福建汀州知府。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as prefect of Tingzhou, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1814 he was posted as prefect of Tingzhou in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 寧化民斂錢集會，大吏將治以叛逆。

translations.literal: The people of Ninghua collected money for gatherings; senior officials were about to treat them as rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Ninghua commoners pooled money for a public gathering, superiors were ready to prosecute them for treason.

sentences.zh: 爾準訊無他狀，論誅首要，鮮所株連。

translations.literal: Erzhun tried the case and found no other circumstances; he sentenced and executed the ringleaders, with few implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhun found no evidence of sedition, executed only the ringleaders, and spared most participants.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽法道、江西按察使，調福建，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Salt Law circuit intendant and Jiangxi surveillance commissioner, was transferred to Fujian, and was promoted in place to administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as salt-law intendant and Jiangxi surveillance commissioner, returned to Fujian, and was promoted on the spot to administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，調廣東布政使，擢安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Guangdong administration commissioner and promoted to governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he became Guangdong administration commissioner and was soon appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 河南邪匪邢名章等糾眾竄潁州，檄按察使惠顯率兵馳剿，格殺名章，殲其餘黨。

translations.literal: The heterodox bandits Xing Mingzhang and others of Henan gathered a mob and fled into Yingzhou; Erzhun ordered Surveillance Commissioner Huixian to lead troops in rapid suppression, killed Mingzhang in combat, and annihilated the rest of the party.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan cultists led by Xing Mingzhang rallied a mob and fled into Yingzhou, Erzhun ordered Surveillance Commissioner Huixian to pursue them, killed Mingzhang in battle, and wiped out his followers.

sentences.zh: 蠲緩被災各屬，災甚者賑恤之。

translations.literal: He remitted and deferred taxes in all disaster-struck districts; where the disaster was severe he gave relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted or deferred taxes in stricken districts and provided direct relief where the damage was worst.

sentences.zh: 先是有言賑務積弊，毋得以銀折錢，爾準疏其弗便，仍循舊章。

translations.literal: Previously there had been talk of accumulated abuses in relief work and that silver must not be converted to cash; Erzhun memorialized that this was inconvenient and continued the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When reformers urged that relief funds no longer be paid in silver converted to cash, Erzhun argued the change would do more harm than good and kept the established practice.

sentences.zh: 三年，調福建巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to governor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he was appointed governor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 延、建各屬山徑叢錯，多盜劫，以萬金為緝捕費，連獲賊首置之法，盜風衰息。

translations.literal: In Yan and Jian circuits the mountain paths were tangled and banditry was frequent; he allotted ten thousand taels for pursuit and capture, successively seized bandit chiefs and punished them by law, and the bandit scourge subsided.
translations.idiomatic: In the rugged Yan and Jian districts, banditry was rampant; he allocated ten thousand taels for pursuit, captured successive ringleaders, and broke the back of the outlaw gangs.

sentences.zh: 巡閱台灣，疏言：「台灣南北袤延千餘裡，初抵鹿耳門，可行舟楫。

translations.literal: On an inspection tour of Taiwan he memorialized: "Taiwan extends more than a thousand li north and south; at first one reached Luermen, where boats and oars could pass."
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Taiwan he reported: "The island stretches over a thousand li from north to south; ships once entered through Luermen."

sentences.zh: 嗣增設鹿仔港，而淺狹多沙，內山溪水赴海，別開港在嘉彰間，曰五條港，頗利商船。

translations.literal: Later Luzai Harbor was added, but it was shallow, narrow, and sandy; mountain streams inland flow to the sea, and a separate port was opened between Jia and Zhang called Wutiao Harbor, which greatly benefits merchant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Luzai Harbor was later added, but it proved shallow and silty; as mountain streams reached the sea, a new port opened between Jia and Zhang—Wutiao Harbor—better suited to merchant shipping.

sentences.zh: 又噶瑪蘭山峻路險，負戴難行，其地有烏石港、加禮遠港，可通五六百石小舟，皆宜設為正口。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Gamlan the mountains are steep and the roads perilous, making porterage difficult; the region has Wushi Harbor and Jialiyuan Harbor, which can accommodate small boats of five or six hundred piculs capacity—all suitable to be established as official ports.
translations.idiomatic: Gamlan, with its steep trails unsuited to overland transport, has Wushi and Jialiyuan harbors that can take boats of five or six hundred piculs; both should be made official ports.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1825 he was appointed governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 奏請噶瑪蘭收入版藉，設官治理。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Gamlan be brought under the civil register and officials appointed to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to bring Gamlan under regular administration and appoint officials to govern it.

sentences.zh: 彰化匪徒械鬥焚劫，旁近蜂起，全台震動，檄水師提督許松年剿捕，副將邵永福等趨艋舺，阻其北竄；

translations.literal: Bandits in Zhanghua fought with weapons, burned, and plundered; neighboring areas rose in swarms and all Taiwan was shaken; he ordered Naval Commander Xu Songnian to suppress and capture them, and Brigadier Shao Yongfu and others hastened to Mengjia to block their flight north;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhanghua brawlers burned and looted and unrest spread across the island, he ordered Naval Commander Xu Songnian to suppress them while Brigadier Shao Yongfu rushed to Mengjia to block a northern breakout;

sentences.zh: 總兵陳化成以兵渡鹿仔，防其入海。

translations.literal: Major General Chen Huacheng crossed at Luzai with troops to prevent their escape to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Major General Chen Huacheng crossed at Luzai with troops to keep them from fleeing by sea.

sentences.zh: 爾準親駐廈門，遣副將佟樞等分往彰化、淡水，搜山圍捕，诇知賊黨煽誘日眾，移陸路提督馬濟勝守廈門，自渡海駐彰化督剿，賊首李通遁，捕得伏誅。

translations.literal: Erzhun personally stationed at Xiamen and sent Brigadiers Tong Shu and others separately to Zhanghua and Tamsui to search the mountains and encircle and capture; intelligence showed the bandit party's incitement and enticement daily growing; he shifted Land Route Commander Ma Jisheng to guard Xiamen, crossed the sea himself to station at Zhanghua to supervise suppression, the bandit chief Li Tong fled, was captured and executed by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhun took post at Xiamen and sent Brigadier Tong Shu and others into Zhanghua and Tamsui to sweep the hills; learning that rebel ranks were swelling daily, he left Land Route Commander Ma Jisheng at Xiamen, crossed to Zhanghua to direct operations himself, and eventually captured and executed the fugitive leader Li Tong.

sentences.zh: 令各莊舉首事，緝餘匪，閩人捕閩人，粵人捕粵人，以免誣累。

translations.literal: He ordered each village to elect headmen to pursue the remaining bandits: Fujianese to arrest Fujianese, Cantonese to arrest Cantonese, so as to avoid false implication.
translations.idiomatic: He had each village elect leaders to hunt down stragglers—Fujianese arresting Fujianese and Cantonese arresting Cantonese—to prevent wrongful accusations across community lines.

sentences.zh: 台人有與生番貿易遂娶番婦者，俗名「番割」，其魁黃斗乃等久踞三灣，潛出為盜。

translations.literal: Some Taiwanese who traded with raw tribes and then married tribal women were popularly called "fan'ge"; their leader Huang Dounai and others had long occupied Sanwan and secretly went out to rob.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwanese who traded with aboriginal tribes and married tribal women were known as "fan'ge"; their leader Huang Dounai had long dominated Sanwan and raided from the hills.

sentences.zh: 當亂起時，誘生番出山助鬥，遣參將黃其漢等分路偵擊。

translations.literal: When the disturbance broke out they induced the raw tribes to come out of the mountains to help fight; he sent Colonel Huang Qihan and others along separate routes to scout and strike.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began they incited aboriginal allies to join the fighting; Erzhun sent Colonel Huang Qihan and others along separate routes to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 番竄後山，士卒攀藤躡葛而登，擒黃斗乃等二十一人，斬以徇。

translations.literal: The tribes fled to the rear mountains; soldiers climbed by grasping vines and treading creepers, captured Huang Dounai and twenty others, and beheaded them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes fled into the back hills; soldiers climbed vine by vine, seized Huang Dounai and twenty-one others, and executed them as an example.

sentences.zh: 爾準疏陳匪徒起事，由於造謠焚掠，非叛逆，當以強盜論；

translations.literal: Erzhun memorialized that the bandits' rising arose from rumor-mongering, burning, and plundering, not rebellion, and should be treated as brigandage;
translations.idiomatic: Erzhun argued that the unrest stemmed from rumor, arson, and looting—not treason—and should be prosecuted as ordinary brigandage;

sentences.zh: 淡水以北分黨報復，當以械鬥論；

translations.literal: north of Tamsui, factional parties took revenge—this should be treated as armed brawling;
translations.idiomatic: north of Tamsui, where factions settled scores by force, cases should be treated as armed brawls;

sentences.zh: 焚殺有據者始坐闢，餘俱末減。

translations.literal: only those with evidence of burning and killing should be charged with sedition; the rest all received reduced sentences.
translations.idiomatic: only those proved to have burned and killed faced sedition charges; all others received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 其脅從旋解散者，多所保全。

translations.literal: Those coerced who soon dispersed were largely spared.
translations.idiomatic: Many who had been coerced and soon dispersed were spared.

sentences.zh: 又奏台灣北路至艋舺幾五百里，僅有守備一員，巡防難週。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that from Taiwan's northern route to Mengjia was nearly five hundred li, with only one garrison commander—it was hard to patrol thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that the northern route from Taiwan to Mengjia ran nearly five hundred li with only one garrison commander—too thin to patrol effectively.

sentences.zh: 調南路游擊一員駐竹塹，並於大甲、銅鑼灣、鬥換坪諸處添駐營汛，改建淡水土城。

translations.literal: He transferred one brigade from the southern route to station at Zhubei, added garrison posts at Dajia, Tongluowan, Douhuanping, and other places, and rebuilt the Tamsui earthen wall.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted a southern-route brigade to Zhubei, added posts at Dajia, Tongluowan, and Douhuanping, and rebuilt Tamsui's earthen fortifications.

sentences.zh: 頭道溪為生番出入總路，亦建土城，以屯丁駐守。

translations.literal: Toudao Creek was the main route by which raw tribes entered and left; an earthen wall was also built there, garrisoned by military colonists.
translations.idiomatic: At Toudao Creek, the main aboriginal thoroughfare, he built another earthen fort manned by military colonists.

sentences.zh: 事平，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，入覲，宣宗嘉其治台灣匪亂悉合機宜，迅速蕆功，賜其子慧翼官主事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he came to court for audience; the Daoguang Emperor praised his handling of the Taiwan bandit disturbance as entirely fitting the occasion and swiftly completed, and granted his son Huiyi the office of director in a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1827 he presented himself at court; the Daoguang Emperor praised his Taiwan campaign as timely and decisive and granted his son Huiyi a directorship in the civil service.

sentences.zh: 木蘭陂者，創自宋熙寧間，溉民田四十萬畝，築石堤千一百餘丈以御海潮，歲久傾壞，爾準道經莆田，親勘修復。

translations.literal: The Mulan Barrage was created in the Xining era of Song, irrigating four hundred thousand mu of commoners' fields; a stone dike of more than eleven hundred zhang was built to resist the sea tide; after years it collapsed and was ruined; Erzhun passed through Putian on his route and personally inspected and restored it.
translations.idiomatic: The Mulan Barrage, built under the Song emperor Shenzong, had irrigated four hundred thousand mu and been shielded by an eleven-hundred-zhang stone seawall until it fell into ruin; passing through Putian, Erzhun surveyed and restored it himself.

sentences.zh: 工蕆，以宋長樂室女錢創陂實功首，建祠列入祀典。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, because the Changle maiden Qian of Song had truly been the first to create the barrage, a shrine was built and she was entered in the sacrificial register.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he built a shrine to the Song-era Changle woman surnamed Qian who had first built the barrage and enrolled her in the official register of sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 爾準治閩最久，諳悉其風土人情，吏民皆相習，政從寬大，閩人安之。

translations.literal: Erzhun governed Fujian longest, was thoroughly versed in its local customs and human feelings, officials and people were all mutually accustomed, his policy followed leniency, and the people of Fujian were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Having governed Fujian longer than any other post, Erzhun knew its customs intimately; officials and commoners alike were used to him, his rule was lenient, and the Fujianese were content.

sentences.zh: 九年，坐失察家僕收賄，鐫二級留任。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was penalized for failure to supervise his household servants' acceptance of bribes, demoted two grades, and retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1829 he was demoted two ranks but kept in office for failing to prevent his servants from taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831 he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒，贈太子太師，賜子慧惇進士，慧翼員外郎，諡文靖，祀福建名宦及鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: The next year he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, his son Huidun was granted metropolitan graduate status, Huiyi was made vice director, his posthumous title was Wenjing, and he was enshrined in Fujian's shrines to famous officials and local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; his son Huidun received metropolitan graduate honors, Huiyi was made vice director, his posthumous name was Wenjing, and he was enshrined among Fujian's eminent officials and local worthies.

sentences.zh: 程祖洛，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Cheng Zuluo was a native of She County, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zuluo came from She County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，授刑部主事，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign he became a metropolitan graduate, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and was promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in 1799, was posted as a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and rose by successive promotions to director.

sentences.zh: 諳練刑名，為仁宗所知。

translations.literal: He was thoroughly versed in penal nomenclature and became known to the Jiaqing Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in criminal law and procedure, he came to the Jiaqing Emperor's attention.

sentences.zh: 京察記名道府，久未外簡，以截取銓授甘肅平涼知府。

translations.literal: In the metropolitan evaluation he was registered for circuit intendant and prefect posts; long without provincial appointment, through intercept appointment he was granted the prefecture of Pingliang in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Listed in the metropolitan review for promotion to circuit-level posts, he went years without a provincial appointment until an exceptional selection made him prefect of Pingliang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 部臣請留，詔斥規避邊遠，撤銷記名，留部永不外用。

translations.literal: The ministry officials requested that he be retained; an edict rebuked him for shirking remote borderlands, revoked his registered name, and detained him in the capital never to serve outside again.
translations.idiomatic: When ministry officials asked to keep him in Beijing, the throne rebuked him for avoiding remote service, struck his name from the promotion list, and ordered that he remain at the capital for life without provincial appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Grand Secretariat Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was made a Grand Secretariat Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 尋授江西按察使，遷湖南布政使，調山東。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Jiangxi Surveillance Commissioner, transferred to Hunan Financial Commissioner, and reassigned to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi, then financial commissioner of Hunan, and was transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，擢陝西巡撫，調河南。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Daoguang reign he was promoted to Shaanxi governor-general and transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was made governor of Shaanxi and then transferred to Henan.

sentences.zh: 教匪硃麻子由新蔡竄安徽阜陽，捕獲置之法。

translations.literal: The sect bandit Zhu Mazi fled from Xincai into Fuyang, Anhui; he was captured and executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhu Mazi, a sectarian outlaw, fled from Xincai into Anhui's Fuyang; Cheng caught him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 與直隸、山東、安徽、湖北毗連諸縣素多盜，撥庫帑五萬兩生息，為緝捕經費。

translations.literal: The counties adjoining Zhili, Shandong, Anhui, and Hubei had long been rife with bandits; he allocated fifty thousand taels from the treasury to earn interest as funds for pursuit and capture.
translations.idiomatic: For counties bordering Zhili, Shandong, Anhui, and Hubei, where banditry was chronic, he set aside fifty thousand taels from the treasury to invest for interest as a standing fund for police operations.

sentences.zh: 漳水決安陽樊馬坊，河流北徙，命大學士戴均元往會勘。

translations.literal: The Zhang River burst at Fanmafang in Anyang; the stream shifted north; the Grand Secretariat member Dai Junyuan was ordered to go jointly to survey.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhang River broke through at Fanmafang in Anyang and shifted northward, the court sent Grand Secretary Dai Junyuan to inspect the breach jointly with local officials.

sentences.zh: 祖洛週曆上下游，合疏言：「漳水自乾隆五十九年南徙合洹以來，衛水為所遏，每致潰溢。

translations.literal: Zuluo personally toured up and down the stream and together submitted a memorial saying: "Since the fifty-ninth year of the Qianlong reign, when the Zhang shifted south and merged with the Huan, the Wei River has been obstructed by it, repeatedly causing breaches and overflows.
translations.idiomatic: Zuluo toured the river personally and jointly memorialized: "Since 1794, when the Zhang shifted south to join the Huan, it has repeatedly blocked and backed up the Wei, causing floods.

sentences.zh: 今河流既分，不可使復合。

translations.literal: Now that the rivers have parted, they must not be allowed to reunite.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the channels have separated, they must not be allowed to merge again.

sentences.zh: 議於樊馬坊上下距洹水最近處，及南岸衝決成溝，並築土壩，使二河分流，冀減漫溢之勢。

translations.literal: It was proposed that at the points above and below Fanmafang nearest to the Huan, and where the southern bank had burst into a gully, earthen dams be built together so the two rivers would divide their flow, hoping to reduce the force of inundation.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed building earthen dams at the places nearest the Huan above and below Fanmafang and along the breached southern bank, so the two rivers would flow separately and reduce flooding.

sentences.zh: 」至四年春，積水消涸，地形顯露。

translations.literal: " By the spring of the fourth year the pooled water dried away and the land's shape was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: " By the spring of 1824 the floods had subsided and the terrain was visible again.

sentences.zh: 田市之北，漫水與溝隔斷，不能引歸正河。

translations.literal: North of Tianshi, the spread water was separated from the ditch and could not be led back into the proper channel.
translations.idiomatic: North of Tianshi, floodwater had been cut off from the ditch and could not be returned to the main channel.

sentences.zh: 乃就其上游龍家莊窪地抽溝啟放，复於內黃馬家窪開引河，添築田家營大壩，使溜勢南趨。

translations.literal: Thereupon at its upper reach at the low ground of Longjiazhuang a ditch was drawn to release water; again at Majiawa in Neihuang a diversion channel was opened; and the great dike at Tianjiaying was added, making the current's force trend south.
translations.idiomatic: He then dug a drainage channel from the low ground at Longjiazhuang upstream, opened a diversion at Majiawa in Neihuang, and reinforced the great dike at Tianjiaying to drive the current southward.

sentences.zh: 自是漳、衛合併之患遂息。

translations.literal: From this the affliction of Zhang and Wei merging was then quelled.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the chronic problem of the Zhang and Wei merging was ended.

sentences.zh: 虞城橫河、惠民溝，夏邑巴清河，永城減水溝，舊為豫東宣洩潦水要區，迭經黃河漫淤，濱河連歲被災，並疏濬之。

translations.literal: Yu City's Heng River, Huimin Ditch, Xiayi's Baqing River, and Yongcheng's Jianshui Ditch had formerly been key zones in eastern Henan for discharging floodwater; repeatedly silted by Yellow River overflows, riverside areas suffered disaster year after year; all were dredged and cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The Heng River at Yucheng, Huimin Ditch, the Baqing River at Xiayi, and Yongcheng's flood-cut channel had long been eastern Henan's main drainage routes; repeated Yellow River silting had left the riverside counties flooded year after year, and he had them all dredged.

sentences.zh: 初，河南、安徽治捻匪從重典，嗣部議有所減改。

translations.literal: Initially Henan and Anhui treated Nian bandits under severe statutes; afterward the ministry deliberated and made reductions and changes.
translations.idiomatic: At first Henan and Anhui had applied the severest penalties to Nian bandits, but the ministry later moved to lighten some provisions.

sentences.zh: 祖洛疏言：「匪徒結捻，倡劫黨眾，一呼而集，其豫謀早在結捻之時。

translations.literal: Zuluo submitted a memorial saying: "When bandits form Nian associations, incite robbery, and rally the party at a single call, their premeditation lay long ago at the time of forming the association.
translations.idiomatic: Zuluo memorialized: "Outlaws who form Nian bands and incite raids can muster a crowd at a shout—their conspiracy begins the moment they organize.

sentences.zh: 新例以是否豫謀分別輕重，諸多窒礙，請復舊例。

translations.literal: The new statute distinguishes severity by whether there was premeditation; in many places it is obstructive; please restore the old statute.
translations.idiomatic: The new law's distinction based on premeditation creates too many obstacles; I ask that the old statute be restored.

sentences.zh: 」並論匪徒拒捕及捕人治罪各條。

translations.literal: " He also discussed the various articles on bandits resisting arrest and punishments for arresting officers.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the articles governing resistance to arrest and punishment of those who made arrests.

sentences.zh: 又言：「獲盜究出舊案，免究從前失察處分。

translations.literal: He also said: "When captured bandits are traced to old cases, waive investigation of prior failure-to-supervise penalties.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued: "When a captured thief reveals an older case, officials should not be penalized for earlier failures of supervision.

sentences.zh: 請遵嘉慶間諭旨，俾除瞻顧。

translations.literal: Please follow the edicts of the Jiaqing period, so as to remove looking-over-one's-shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the Jiaqing edicts on this point, so that officials need not look over their shoulders."

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: " All was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 七年，丁母憂，服闋，署工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he mourned his mother; when mourning ended he served as acting vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1827 he mourned his mother; after the mourning period he served as acting vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋署湖南巡撫，調江蘇。

translations.literal: Shortly he served as acting Hunan governor-general and was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon acting governor of Hunan, then transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 命查辦浙江鹽務，嚴定裁汰浮費章程，下部議行。

translations.literal: He was ordered to investigate and handle Zhejiang salt administration, strictly fixing regulations to pare superfluous expenses, and submitted them to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to investigate Zhejiang's salt monopoly, drew up strict rules to cut wasteful spending, and had them sent to the ministry for approval.

sentences.zh: 台灣奸民張丙、陳辦等倡亂，命將軍瑚松額督兵進剿，祖洛專治後路軍需。

translations.literal: Taiwan scoundrels Zhang Bing, Chen Ban, and others incited rebellion; the general Husonge was ordered to supervise troops in pursuit; Zuluo solely managed rear-line military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bing, Chen Ban, and other ruffians raised a rebellion in Taiwan, General Husonge was sent to command the campaign while Zuluo handled logistics.

sentences.zh: 十三年，提督馬濟勝破賊，張丙等就擒，赴台灣籌辦善後事宜，劾戰守不力之都司週進龍等，褫黜有差。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the provincial military commander Ma Jisheng defeated the bandits; Zhang Bing and others were captured; he went to Taiwan to arrange postwar affairs, impeached commanders such as Zhou Jinlong of the rank of commander for inadequate defense and attack, and dismissed or degraded them by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In 1833, after Provincial Commander Ma Jisheng defeated the rebels and captured Zhang Bing, Zuluo went to Taiwan to handle reconstruction, impeached negligent commanders including Zhou Jinlong, and demoted them as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 改營製，增防守。

translations.literal: He reformed camp regulations and increased defense.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the garrison system and strengthened coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 優敘，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He received favorable merit review and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He received an exceptional merit citation and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 疏陳福建吏治，略曰：「安民必先懲蠹，不可以回護瞻顧而曲縱奸惡。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth Fujian officialdom, stating in summary: "To secure the people one must first punish parasites; one cannot through shielding and looking-over-one's-shoulder bend the law to indulge wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial on Fujian governance he wrote in essence: "To pacify the people you must first punish corruption; you cannot wink at wickedness out of favoritism or fear.

sentences.zh: 閩省吏治無子惠之政，而務寬大之名，始因官之庸劣，釀成頑梗之風，今又因民之譸張，遂有疲難之勢。

translations.literal: Fujian provincial officialdom has no policy of cherishing the people, yet pursues a reputation for leniency; at first because officials were mediocre and incompetent a stubborn and obstinate wind was brewed; now again because the people exaggerate and distort, there is a weary and difficult situation.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian administration has no real concern for the people yet prides itself on leniency; mediocre officials first bred obstinacy among the populace, and now popular exaggeration has made governance nearly unmanageable.

sentences.zh: 官曰民刁，民曰吏虐，互相傳播，漸失其真。

translations.literal: Officials say the people are crafty; the people say the clerks are brutal; each side spreads this, and gradually the truth is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Officials call the people difficult; the people call the officials cruel—each side repeats the charge until no one can tell truth from rumor.

sentences.zh: 官不執法，幕不守法，因而愚民犯法，書役弄法，棍徒玩法。

translations.literal: Officials do not enforce the law, secretaries do not observe the law, and thereby ignorant people break the law, clerks manipulate the law, and ruffians play with the law.
translations.idiomatic: When magistrates will not enforce the law and their secretaries ignore it, commoners break the law in ignorance, yamen clerks twist it, and thugs exploit it.

sentences.zh: 必先懲不執法之官，然後能治犯法、弄法、玩法之人。

translations.literal: One must first punish officials who do not enforce the law, and only then can one govern those who break, manipulate, and play with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Punish officials who will not enforce the law first, and only then can you deal with those who break, twist, or abuse it."

sentences.zh: 」於是連劾官吏不職者，略無假貸，吏治始肅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he impeached derelict officials in succession, granting almost no indulgence, and officialdom was first brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached a series of incompetent officials without leniency, and administration began to improve.

sentences.zh: 已革縣丞秦師韓京控提督馬濟勝矇奏邀功，並訐祖洛偏袒欺矇，命侍郎趙盛奎偕學攻張鱗按鞫，白其誣，師韓遣戍新疆。

translations.literal: The dismissed assistant magistrate Qin Shihan memorialized from the capital accusing Provincial Commander Ma Jisheng of deceitful memorials to claim merit, and also charging Zuluo with partiality and deception; the vice minister Zhao Shengkui was ordered together with the Hanlin examiner Zhang Lin to investigate; his false charges were cleared; Shihan was banished to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed assistant magistrate Qin Shihan appealed to Beijing accusing Ma Jisheng of inflating his reports and Zuluo of covering for him; Vice Minister Zhao Shengkui and Hanlin examiner Zhang Lin were sent to investigate, found the charges false, and banished Shihan to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，疏陳閩洋形勢，以漳州之南澳、銅山為籓籬，泉之廈門、金門為門戶，興化之海壇為右翼，閩安為省會咽喉，福寧之銅山為後戶。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he submitted a memorial setting forth the situation of Fujian's seas: taking Nan'ao and Tongshan of Zhangzhou as outer fence, Xiamen and Kinmen of Quanzhou as gates, Haitan of Xinghua as right wing, Min'an as the province's throat, and Tongshan of Funing as rear gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he memorialized on Fujian's coastal defenses: Nan'ao and Tongshan off Zhangzhou as the outer barrier, Xiamen and Kinmen as the gates, Haitan off Xinghua as the right flank, Min'an as the capital's throat, and Funing's Tongshan as the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 巡緝守禦，全資寨城砲台。

translations.literal: Patrol, pursuit, and defense relied entirely on stockade towns and artillery platforms.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal patrol and defense depended wholly on stockades and gun batteries.

sentences.zh: 就最要者四十四處，由官民捐貲修築。

translations.literal: At the forty-four most critical places, officials and commoners donated funds for repair and construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the forty-four most critical sites, officials and local donors funded repairs.

sentences.zh: 十六年，丁父憂去官，服闋，引疾不出。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he left office on mourning his father; when mourning ended he cited illness and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 he left office to mourn his father; after mourning he pleaded illness and declined further service.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，宣宗甚惜之，贈太子太保，諡簡敬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died; the Daoguang Emperor deeply regretted it; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Jianjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1848; the Daoguang Emperor mourned the loss, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Jianjing.

sentences.zh: 馬濟勝，山東菏澤人。

translations.literal: Ma Jisheng was a native of Heze, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jisheng came from Heze in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以武生入伍，從剿川、陝教匪，積功累擢江蘇撫標參將。

translations.literal: As a military licentiate he entered the ranks, followed in suppressing Sichuan and Shaanxi sect bandits, and through accumulated merit was repeatedly promoted to Jiangsu provincial battalion colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Entering service as a military licentiate, he fought the sectarian rebels in Sichuan and Shaanxi and rose by accumulated merit to colonel in the Jiangsu provincial army.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年，會剿山東教匪，擢河北鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing he joined in suppressing Shandong sect bandits and was promoted to commander of Hebei Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he helped suppress the Shandong sectarians and was made commander of the Hebei garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光初，擢浙江提督，調福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang he was promoted to Zhejiang provincial military commander and transferred to Fujian land-route provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he was made provincial commander of Zhejiang, then transferred to the Fujian land forces.

sentences.zh: 張丙等倡亂嘉義，台灣鎮總兵劉廷斌困守孤城。

translations.literal: Zhang Bing and others incited disorder in Jiayi; Taiwan garrison commander Liu Tingbin was trapped defending a lone city.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bing and his followers rebelled at Jiayi, Taiwan Garrison Commander Liu Tingbin was besieged in the city.

sentences.zh: 濟勝率兵二千渡海赴援，戰於嘉義城下，大破賊，追至蘋港尾，擒斬甚眾；

translations.literal: Jisheng led two thousand troops across the sea to relieve them, fought below Jiayi city, greatly defeated the bandits, pursued to Pinggangwei, and captured and beheaded a great number;
translations.idiomatic: Jisheng led two thousand men across the strait, routed the rebels below Jiayi, pursued them to Pinggangwei, and killed or captured a great many;

sentences.zh: 進屯鹽水港，分兵搜剿，張丙及其悍黨先後就擒。

translations.literal: he advanced to garrison at Yanshui Harbor, divided troops to search and suppress, and Zhang Bing and his fierce partisans were captured in succession.
translations.idiomatic: advanced to Yanshui Harbor, sent columns to hunt the remainder, and captured Zhang Bing and his chief lieutenants.

sentences.zh: 時命將軍瑚松額督師猶未至，詔褒成功迅速，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: At the time the ordered general Husonge to command the army had still not arrived; an edict praised the swift success and granted double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: General Husonge, the designated supreme commander, had not yet arrived; the throne praised Jisheng's speed and awarded him the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 餘匪萬餘復來犯，俟其怠，擊之大潰，擒頭目賴滿等，追剿盡毀其巢，賊遂平。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand remnant bandits again came to attack; waiting until they grew weary, he struck and they were greatly routed; ringleaders such as Lai Man were captured; pursuit and suppression completely destroyed their nests, and the bandits were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When more than ten thousand holdouts attacked again, he waited until they tired, smashed them in one blow, captured leaders including Lai Man, destroyed their bases in pursuit, and the rebellion was ended.

sentences.zh: 宣宗深嘉其謀勇，錫封二等男爵。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor deeply praised his strategy and courage and granted enfeoffment as second-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor greatly admired his skill and courage and ennobled him as a second-class baron.

sentences.zh: 又以馭兵安靖，御書「忠勇廉明」四字賜之。

translations.literal: Also because he governed troops in tranquility, the imperial brush wrote four characters "Loyal, Brave, Incorrupt, Clear" and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: For governing his troops with discipline and calm, the emperor wrote him the four characters "Loyal, Brave, Incorrupt, and Clear."

sentences.zh: 召入覲，年逾七旬，猶壯健，溫詔褒獎，晉二等子爵，在御前侍衛上行走。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, though past seventy he was still robust; a warm edict praised and rewarded him; he was advanced to second-rank viscount and served in the Imperial Bodyguard above walking rank.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court at over seventy, still vigorous, he received a warm commendation, was raised to second-class viscount, and was appointed to serve in the Imperial Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒於官，贈太子太保，諡昭武，四子皆予官。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died in office; posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Zhaowu, and all four sons were granted offices.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1836, was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Zhaowu, and all four sons received official appointments.

sentences.zh: 裕泰，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Yu Tai was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tai was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 由官學生考授內閣中書，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: From Imperial Academy student he passed examination and received appointment as Grand Secretariat secretary, and was transferred to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: A graduate of the Imperial Academy, he passed the examination for Grand Secretariat secretary and was later made reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶末，出為四川成綿龍茂道，歷四川、湖南、安徽按察使，湖南、陝西、安徽布政使。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiaqing he went out as Sichuan Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao circuit intendant, served successively as Sichuan, Hunan, and Anhui surveillance commissioner, and Hunan, Shaanxi, and Anhui financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jiaqing reign he was sent out as intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao circuit in Sichuan, then served as surveillance commissioner in Sichuan, Hunan, and Anhui and as financial commissioner in Hunan, Shaanxi, and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年，擢盛京刑部侍郎，調工部，兼管奉天府尹事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he was promoted to Mukden Ministry of Justice vice minister, transferred to Works, and concurrently managed Fengtian prefectural administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831 he became vice minister of justice at Mukden, moved to the Ministry of Works, and concurrently oversaw the Fengtian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 查勘科爾沁蒙旗荒地，奏禁私墾。

translations.literal: He surveyed wasteland in the Khorchin Mongol banners and memorialized to forbid private reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed wasteland in the Khorchin banners and memorialized to ban unauthorized cultivation.

sentences.zh: 十三年，召授刑部侍郎，尋出為貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned and appointed vice minister of Justice; shortly he went out as Guizhou governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1833 he was recalled to be vice minister of Justice, then sent out as governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，古州、黎平土匪起，擒其渠徐玉貴等誅之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year bandits rose in Juzhou and Liping; he captured their chieftain Xu Yugui and others and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 rebels rose in Juzhou and Liping; he captured their leader Xu Yugui and others and executed them.

sentences.zh: 調湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hunan governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 鎮筸標兵滋事，劾總兵向遵化、辰沅道常慶不職，罷之。

translations.literal: Zhenbian battalion troops caused trouble; he impeached commander Xiang Zunhua and Chen-Yuan circuit intendant Chang Qing for dereliction and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhenbian garrison mutinied, he impeached Commander Xiang Zunhua and Chen-Yuan intendant Chang Qing for negligence and removed them.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「苗疆屯田，嘉慶中道員傅鼐所經營，寓兵於農，籌邊良策。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Miao frontier military colonies, managed in Jiaqing by circuit intendant Fu Nai, quartered troops within farming—an excellent border policy.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The Miao frontier colonies that Intendant Fu Nai established in the Jiaqing era, combining farming with garrison duty, were an excellent border policy.

sentences.zh: 治安日久，諸弊叢生。

translations.literal: Long peace and order have bred many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Long peace has bred many abuses.

sentences.zh: 今鎮筸標兵因借餉倡亂，苗人遂生觀望。

translations.literal: Now Zhenbian battalion troops stirred trouble over borrowed pay, and the Miao consequently grew watchful and hesitant.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenbian mutiny over borrowed pay has made the Miao watchful.

sentences.zh: 重以苗官苛刻，屯長侵欺，後患堪虞。

translations.literal: Added to this Miao officials are harsh, colony headmen encroach and cheat, and future troubles are to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh Miao officials and corrupt colony headmen make future trouble likely.

sentences.zh: 急應清釐損益，妥定章程，俾將弁兵練咸知經費有常，絕其覬覦，仍責成鎮道實力整飭，恩威並行。

translations.literal: Urgently one should clear and weigh gains and losses, properly fix regulations, so that officers and troops all know funds are regular and end their coveting, while still charging the garrison commander and circuit intendant to discipline in earnest, combining grace and majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Reforms and clear rules are urgently needed so officers and men know their pay is secure, ambitions are checked, and garrison commanders enforce discipline with both rewards and punishments."

sentences.zh: 」尋議定苗疆兵勇不准客民充補，預借銀穀限以定制，拔補備弁屯長，嚴絕苞苴。

translations.literal: " Shortly regulations were fixed: Miao-frontier soldiers might not be filled by outsider commoners; advance borrowing of silver and grain was limited to established amounts; supplementary appointment of deputy officers and colony headmen was tightened; gifts and bribery were strictly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations soon followed: outsider recruits were barred from Miao garrisons, advances on pay were capped, colony officers were appointed by merit, and bribery was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 辰沅道缺，以湖南知府題升。

translations.literal: The Chen-Yuan circuit post was vacant; a Hunan prefect was nominated for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen-Yuan intendant's post was filled by promoting a Hunan prefect.

sentences.zh: 並如所議行。

translations.literal: All was implemented as deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: All was carried out as proposed.

sentences.zh: 十七年，調江西，復調湖南。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to Jiangxi, then again transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he was transferred to Jiangxi, then back to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Huguang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1840 he was made governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，湖北崇陽逆匪鍾人傑作亂，踞縣城，陷通城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Hubei Chongyang rebel bandit Zhong Renjie made disorder, occupied the county seat, and seized Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 the rebel Zhong Renjie rose at Chongyang in Hubei, seized the county seat, and took Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 裕泰馳駐咸寧，檄按察使郭熊飛率都司玉貴等進剿。

translations.literal: Yu Tai hastened to garrison at Xianning and issued orders to Surveillance Commissioner Guo Xiongfei to lead Commander Yugu and others in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tai hurried to Xianning and ordered Surveillance Commissioner Guo Xiongfei and Commander Yugu to advance against them.

sentences.zh: 崇陽在萬山中，賊盡塞孔道，築砦抗拒，選精銳出賊後夾攻，分股犯蒲圻，連為官軍所敗，踞崇陽西嶺為負嵎計。

translations.literal: Chongyang lies amid myriad mountains; the bandits blocked all passes, built stockades to resist, selected crack troops to strike from behind the rebels in pincer attack; they split forces to invade Qibi and were repeatedly defeated by government troops; they held Chongyang's western ridge as a cornered-beast strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyang lies deep in the mountains; the rebels blocked the passes and built fortified stockades. Government forces sent elite troops around their rear while the rebels split off to raid Qibi, were beaten back repeatedly, and held the western ridge of Chongyang as a last stand.

sentences.zh: 提督劉允孝迭敗之石盤山、黑橋，進毀其巢，擒人傑及其黨陳寶銘、汪敦族等。

translations.literal: Provincial commander Liu Yunxiao repeatedly defeated them at Shipanshan and Heiqiao, advanced and destroyed their nests, and captured Renjie and his partisans Chen Baoming, Wang Dunzu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commander Liu Yunxiao defeated them repeatedly at Shipanshan and Heiqiao, destroyed their strongholds, and captured Renjie and his lieutenants Chen Baoming and Wang Dunzu.

sentences.zh: 尋复通城，盡俘其孥。

translations.literal: Shortly Tongcheng was recovered and all their women and children were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Tongcheng was soon retaken and the rebels' families were captured.

sentences.zh: 事平，加太子太保，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利兵由海入江，詔募勇習水戰。

translations.literal: At the time English troops entered the river from the sea; an edict ordered recruiting braves to drill in naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: As British forces advanced up the Yangtze from the sea, the court ordered the recruitment and training of militia for river combat.

sentences.zh: 裕泰仿粵艇造大船六、快船四，簡漢陽水師，每船百人，按旬操練。

translations.literal: Yu Tai modeled Guangdong craft to build six large ships and four fast boats, selected Hankou naval troops, a hundred men per ship, drilling each ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tai built six large junks and four fast boats on the Guangdong model, assigned a hundred Hankou sailors to each, and drilled them every ten days.

sentences.zh: 裁舊有巡船，以節經費。

translations.literal: He cut the old patrol boats to economize funds.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced the old patrol fleet to save funds.

sentences.zh: 荊州駐防每出營滋事，奏請飭地方官拘拿，報將軍秉公嚴懲。

translations.literal: Jingzhou garrison troops whenever leaving camp caused trouble; he memorialized requesting that local officials arrest them and report to the general for impartial severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou garrison troops repeatedly left camp to cause trouble, he asked that local officials arrest them and report to the general for discipline.

sentences.zh: 乾州苗竄擾，剿撫解散。

translations.literal: Qianzhou Miao raided and harassed; he suppressed and pacified them and they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Miao raids from Qianzhou were suppressed by force and conciliation until the groups dispersed.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，李沅發倡亂新寧，踞城戕官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Li Yuanfa incited disorder in Xinning, occupied the city, and killed officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 Li Yuanfa rebelled at Xinning, seized the city, and killed the officials.

sentences.zh: 巡撫馮德馨、提督英俊往剿，复縣城。

translations.literal: Governor Feng Dexin and provincial commander Yingjun went to suppress and recovered the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Feng Dexin and Provincial Commander Yingjun marched against him and retook the county seat.

sentences.zh: 妄傳沅發已死，而賊竄山中，勾結黔、粵交界伏莽，勢益蔓延。

translations.literal: It was falsely rumored Yuanfa was dead, yet the bandits fled into the mountains, linked with hidden braves at the Guizhou-Guangdong border, and their force spread all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Although Yuanfa was falsely reported dead, his men fled into the mountains, linked up with outlaws along the Guizhou-Guangdong border, and the rebellion spread.

sentences.zh: 馮德馨逮治，專任裕泰往督師，與黔、粵諸軍合擊，數捷。

translations.literal: Feng Dexin was arrested and tried; Yu Tai alone was charged to go supervise the army; with Guizhou and Guangdong troops he joined in attack and won several victories.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dexin was arrested; Yu Tai alone directed the campaign, coordinating with Guizhou and Guangdong forces to win several victories.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，搜剿山內，擒殲多名。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirtieth year he searched and suppressed within the mountains and captured and destroyed many.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1850 government forces swept the mountains, killing and capturing many rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊竄永福草奚塘，四面抄圍，漸窮蹙。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Yongfu Caoxitang; on four sides they were encircled and copied, gradually driven to extremity.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Caoxitang in Yongfu, were surrounded on all sides, and grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 裕泰度賊不南趨廣西全州，即入新寧瑤峒，令提督向榮由武岡進屯廣西懷遠，遇賊擊破之。

translations.literal: Yu Tai judged that if the bandits did not hurry south toward Quanzhou in Guangxi they would enter Xinning Yao ravines; he ordered Provincial Commander Xiang Rong from Wugang to advance and garrison at Huaiyuan in Guangxi; encountering the bandits he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting the rebels either to strike south toward Quanzhou in Guangxi or to flee into the Yao hills of Xinning, Yu Tai sent Provincial Commander Xiang Rong from Wugang to station at Huaiyuan in Guangxi, where he met and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊退踞金峰嶺，分三路進擊於深箐陡石間，斬獲殆盡，沅發就擒，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated to hold Jinfeng Ridge; advancing in three routes within deep ravines and steep stone they were beheaded and captured nearly to the last; Yuanfa was captured; he was advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Jinfeng Ridge; a three-pronged assault through the steep ravines killed or captured nearly all of them, Yuanfa was taken, and Yu Tai was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，調陝甘，入覲，卒，優詔以尚書例賜卹，諡莊毅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu; he entered audience and died; a favorable edict granted condolence at ministerial standard, posthumous title Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu, presented himself at court, and died; the throne granted minister-level funeral honors with the posthumous name Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: 子長善，廣州將軍；

translations.literal: His son Changshan, Guangzhou general;
translations.idiomatic: His son Changshan became general of Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 長敘，侍郎。

translations.literal: Changxu, vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Changxu became a vice minister.

sentences.zh: 賀長齡，字耦耕，湖南善化人，原籍浙江會稽。

translations.literal: He Zhangling, style name Ougeng, was a native of Shanhua, Hunan, with original domicile in Kuaiji, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhangling, whose style name was Ougeng, was registered in Shanhua, Hunan, though his family came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 高祖上振，官湖南司獄，卹囚有隱德，貧未能歸，遂家湖南。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shangzhen served as Hunan prison intendant, showed hidden virtue in pitying prisoners, was too poor to return home, and thus the family settled in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shangzhen, a Hunan prison intendant known for humane treatment of inmates, was too poor to return to Zhejiang, and the family made its home in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 長齡，嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷贊善。

translations.literal: Zhangling, a metropolitan graduate of the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, was selected as Hanlin Bachelor, appointed compiler, and promoted to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangling passed the metropolitan examination in 1808, entered the Hanlin Academy, became a compiler, and was promoted to tutor in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，出為江西南昌知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Nanchang, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was posted as prefect of Nanchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 歷山東兗沂曹濟道、江蘇按察使，就遷布政使，佐巡撫陶澍創行海運。

translations.literal: He served as Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji circuit intendant in Shandong and Jiangsu surveillance commissioner, was promoted in place to administration commissioner, and assisted Governor Tao Zhu in inaugurating sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: He served as intendant of the Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji circuit in Shandong and as Jiangsu surveillance commissioner, then became administration commissioner and helped Governor Tao Zhu launch grain transport by sea.

sentences.zh: 調山東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1827 he served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 臨清州教匪馬進忠為逆伏誅，復有揭帖偽立名號，刻期舉事，臚列旁州縣民名數百。

translations.literal: The Linqing sect bandit Ma Jinzhong had been executed for rebellion; afterward placards falsely set up names and fixed a date for action, listing several hundred commoners' names from neighboring prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: After the Linqing sect rebel Ma Jinzhong was executed, anonymous placards named hundreds of people in neighboring counties and set a date for an uprising.

sentences.zh: 長齡曰：「謀不軌詎以姓名月日告？

translations.literal: Zhangling said: "Would conspirators announce their names and the month and day?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhangling said, "Would real conspirators publish their names and the date of their plot?"

sentences.zh: 此移禍也。

translations.literal: This is shifting calamity onto others."
translations.idiomatic: This is an attempt to frame innocent people."

sentences.zh: 」诇知果出邀功者，欲藉興大獄，遂置不問。

translations.literal: " Intelligence showed it indeed came from one seeking merit, who wished to use this to launch a major case; he therefore set it aside.
translations.idiomatic: " Investigation showed the tip came from someone angling for credit and hoping to trigger a mass prosecution; Zhangling ignored it.

sentences.zh: 調江寧布政使，乞歸養親。

translations.literal: Transferred to Jiangning administration commissioner, he requested leave to return home and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Named Jiangning administration commissioner, he asked to retire and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 十五年，母喪服闋，補福建布攻使，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when mourning for his mother ended, he was appointed Fujian administration commissioner and transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning ended in 1835, he became Fujian administration commissioner and was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 he was appointed governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 黔民苦訟累而多盜，以聽斷緝捕課吏，設旬報為考覈。

translations.literal: The people of Qian suffered from litigation burdens and there were many bandits; he made hearing cases and capturing bandits the officials' duties of assessment and set ten-day reports for evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou's people were crushed by lawsuits and banditry was rife; he graded officials on how well they judged cases and caught thieves and required ten-day progress reports.

sentences.zh: 十八年，仁懷奸民穆繼賢糾四川綦江匪肆劫，遣兵與川軍會剿，焚其巢，首從並就殲擒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Renhuai ruffian Mu Jixian gathered Qijiang bandits from Sichuan to plunder; he sent troops to join Sichuan forces in joint suppression, burned their nest, and ringleaders and followers were all destroyed and captured.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 the Renhuai agitator Mu Jixian joined Sichuan bandits from Qijiang in raids; Zhangling sent troops to cooperate with Sichuan forces, burned their base, and killed or captured the leaders and their followers.

sentences.zh: 郎岱、普安、清鎮諸縣多種罌粟，拔除申禁，勸民種木棉，玉屏、婺川皆有成效。

translations.literal: Langdai, Pu'an, and Qingzhen and other counties widely planted opium poppy; he uprooted it and proclaimed the ban, urging the people to plant cotton; Yuping and Wuchuan both had results.
translations.idiomatic: In Langdai, Pu'an, Qingzhen, and other counties opium was widely grown; he uprooted the crops, enforced the ban, and urged farmers to plant cotton—with success in Yuping and Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 黔省安置流犯三千餘人，與苗民錯處，釁隙易生，疏請改發新疆；

translations.literal: In Qian province more than three thousand exiles were settled, living intermixed with Miao people, and friction easily arose; he memorialized requesting they be sent instead to Xinjiang;
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand exiles in Guizhou lived among the Miao and friction was constant; he petitioned to send them to Xinjiang instead;

sentences.zh: 又以鎮遠、黎平、都勻、古州苗俗桀驁，以盜為生，州縣差役緝捕難週，疏請綠營每百名內精選數名，分隸府、廳、州、縣文員管轄，勤加訓練，專司捕盜：並下部議行。
