translations.literal: Moreover, because at Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou Miao customs were fierce and they lived by robbery, and prefectural and county runners found pursuit difficult, he memorialized requesting that from each hundred Green Standard troops several elite men be selected, placed under civil officials of prefectures, departments, and counties, diligently trained, and charged solely with capturing bandits: all was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that in Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou unruly Miao lived by banditry and local runners could not keep up; he asked that elite Green Standard soldiers be picked from each hundred-man unit, placed under civil officials, trained, and used solely for bandit suppression—all referred to the ministries for approval.

sentences.zh: 長齡治黔九載，振興文教，貴陽、銅仁、安順、石阡四府，普安、八寨、郎岱、松桃四廳，黃平、普定，天柱、永從、甕安、清平、興義、普安諸州縣，皆建書院義學；

translations.literal: Zhangling governed Qian for nine years, reviving culture and education; in the four prefectures of Guiyang, Tongren, Anshun, and Shiqian, the four departments of Pu'an, Bazhai, Langdai, and Songtao, and the prefectures and counties of Huangping, Puding, Tianzhu, Yongcong, Weng'an, Qingping, Xingyi, and Pu'an, he all built academies and charity schools;
translations.idiomatic: During nine years governing Guizhou, Zhangling revived education, founding academies and charity schools in Guiyang, Tongren, Anshun, Shiqian, and many departments and counties across the province;

sentences.zh: 省會書院分上內外三舍，親試考覈，刊刻經籍，頒行州縣。

translations.literal: The provincial academy was divided into upper, inner, and outer halls; he personally tested and evaluated, printed classics, and distributed them to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial academy was divided into three halls; he examined students personally, printed classics, and distributed them province-wide.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢雲貴總督，兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrently acted as governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he was made governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and also acted as Yunnan governor.

sentences.zh: 漢、回連歲互鬥，永昌回變敗退後，复圖攻城，城回謀內應，迤西道羅天池悉捕誅之。

translations.literal: Han and Hui had fought year after year; after the Yongchang Hui rising was defeated and retreated, they again plotted to storm the city; Hui within the city plotted to respond from within; Western Yunnan Circuit Intendant Luo Tianchi arrested and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Hui communities had fought for years; after the Yongchang Muslim rising was beaten back, rebels again plotted to storm the city with inside collaborators until Intendant Luo Tianchi arrested and executed the conspirators.

sentences.zh: 長齡親往督剿，擊走叛回，以肅清入告。

translations.literal: Zhangling went in person to supervise suppression, drove off the rebel Hui, and reported the area pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangling went in person to direct operations, drove off the rebels, and reported the region pacified.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，回眾藉口善良不別，复叛，自請議處，撤銷獎敘，赴大理、永昌督剿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Hui masses, taking the pretext that good and wicked were not distinguished, rebelled again; he requested himself for disciplinary action, had rewards revoked, and went to Dali and Yongchang to supervise suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 the Muslims rebelled again, claiming innocents had been lumped with guilty; Zhangling asked to be punished, gave up his honors, and went to Dali and Yongchang to command the campaign.

sentences.zh: 匪尋竄散，請免投誠張富罪，軍犯王芝異團練出力，亦請釋回。

translations.literal: The bandits soon scattered in flight; he requested exemption from punishment for the surrendered Zhang Fu; the military convict Wang Zhiyi had aided the militia and was also requested to be released.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon scattered; he asked clemency for the surrendered Zhang Fu and for the release of Wang Zhiyi, a military convict who had helped the militia.

sentences.zh: 詔斥其庸懦，降補河南布政使。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked his timidity and cowardice and demoted him to Henan administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked his timidity and demoted him to Henan administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 滇回复擾雲州，多屬永昌遺孽，且得羅天池濫殺狀，追論長齡，褫職。

translations.literal: The Yunnan Hui again disturbed Yunzhou, mostly remnants of Yongchang, and moreover the facts of Luo Tianchi's indiscriminate killing came to light; Zhangling was pursued in judgment and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan Muslims raided Yunzhou—mostly Yongchang holdouts—and Luo Tianchi's mass killings came to light, Zhangling was stripped of office in a formal review.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳若霖、戴三錫盡心民事，而三錫久任蜀疆，治效較多。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Chen Ruolin and Dai Sanxi devoted themselves to the people's affairs, but Sanxi long held the Shu frontier and his governing achievements were comparatively greater.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: Chen Ruolin and Dai Sanxi both devoted themselves to civil administration, but Sanxi's long tenure in Sichuan produced the greater record.

sentences.zh: 孫爾準、程祖洛先後治閩有聲，寬嚴殊途，其相濟之道乎？

translations.literal: Sun Erzhun and Cheng Zuluo successively governed Fujian with renown; lenient and strict were different paths—is this their way of complementing each other?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Erzhun and Cheng Zuluo both governed Fujian with distinction—one lenient, one strict—were their different methods complementary?

sentences.zh: 裕泰兩殄楚寇，勳施爛然。

translations.literal: Yu Tai twice exterminated Chu bandits, his merit shining brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tai twice crushed rebellions in Huguang, his achievements conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 賀長齡儒而不武，不足以奠岩疆也。

translations.literal: He Zhangling was a scholar without martial ability, insufficient to secure a rugged frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhangling was a scholar rather than a soldier, ill-suited to hold a troubled frontier.
